timeline.change: Mercedes-Benz becomes preferred tenderer for Australia's Land 121 Overlander project, which includes a 6×6 G-Wagen
G 63 AMG 6×6 shown and driven by press in Dubai; limited production begins at Magna Steyr, Graz
Customer deliveries; MotorTrend reports nearly 60 built by late 2013

identify.intro: Aftermarket six-wheel conversions of ordinary W463s exist and have sold publicly, so prove a truck is a factory 6×6 before paying factory-6×6 money.

items.head: Chassis number
items.body: Factory trucks on Bring a Trailer carry chassis numbers such as WDB4632721X…. Ask for Mercedes build paperwork, and treat a standard G 550/G 63/G 65 VIN on a six-wheeler as a conversion.

items.head: Overhead console
items.body: Factory trucks have tyre-pressure switches, twin air-pressure gauges and an auxiliary fuel gauge in the overhead console.

items.head: Running gear
items.body: Three portal axles, 18-inch two-piece beadlocks, carbon-fibre arch extensions, a stainless roll bar in the bed and compressor tanks in the rear arches.

items.head: Lockers
items.body: Three locker switches that operate five differential locks in stages; MotorTrend notes they engage even in high range.

items.head: US import paperwork
items.body: US trucks should carry an EPA conversion label (G&K Automotive Conversion) and an NHTSA Show or Display exemption letter.

values.intro: These are collector prices with a small market. Brabus trucks and very low mileage add the most, and the restrictions on US Show or Display trucks hold some bids down.
values.note: Based on six Bring a Trailer sales from 2020 to 2026: $901,337 (2020), $1,170,000 (Brabus, 2022), $778,000 (Weistec, 2024), $616,000 (2025), $915,000 (Brabus, January 2026) and $500,000 (May 2026). Bids of $803,633–831,000 did not meet reserve in 2023 and 2026.

paragraphs: Mercedes never sold the G 63 AMG 6×6 in the United States, and MotorTrend said so at launch. Trucks in the US were imported and modified for EPA compliance by G&K Automotive Conversion of Santa Ana, California, and run under NHTSA's Show or Display exemption.

Bring a Trailer listings spell out the conditions: NHTSA must approve every change of ownership, the buyer must apply for a new Show or Display approval with current photos, mileage is limited to 2,500 a year, and the truck must be available for NHTSA inspection until it is at least 25 years old. The earliest 2013 trucks reach 25 years in 2038.
